recipes.name: Split Pea and Ham Bone Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch salt and pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a medium pot, add onions and saute until tender. Stir in split peas, ham bone, and enough water to cover ingredients; season with salt and pepper.
Cover, and cook until there are no peas left, just a green liquid, 2 hours. While it is cooking, check to see if water has evaporated. You may need to add more water as the soup continues to cook.
Once the soup is a green liquid remove from heat, and let stand so it will thicken. Once thickened you may need to heat through to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Split Pea and Ham Bone Soup
raw_recipe.description: This is a straight-forward version of a classic soup combines dried split peas with onion and ham. Variations include adding carrots, celery, or potatoes.

review.reviewBody:
There's a lot you can do with this recipe, beginning with buying the ham bone at any Honey Baked Ham Store--a coupla bucks and they usually leave about a pound of ham on 'em.

I don't brown anything first--just toss in as much diced onion, carrot, celery, and potato as you like. A little garlic adds an interesting dimension. I use a whole bag of dried split peas (not pre-soaked), and after they are cooked and beginning to fall apart, I add another half bag. By the end of the slow cooking time (at least 2 hours; longer is better), the first batch of peas has disintegrated, and the second is soft, cooked, but retains their shape.

Take it easy with the salt because the ham is usually very salty. UPDATE 2/6/20: HBH has discovered that there's quite a market for their hambones. So, they're now $10-15--about the price of a butt or shank ham in the grocery store. Oh well.

Fabulous! I love split pea and ham soup and this proved to be so easy yet so delicious I'll be making it more often than I thought! I soaked my peas overnight and opted for the crock pot method so there was no need for oil. I just put everything into the crock pot using a chopped ham steak vs. a ham bone along with a couple of dashes of liquid smoke and couple of pinches of celery salt vs. salt. I also used 32 oz. of chicken broth vs. water for a richer flavor. I set the crock pot to high for 2 hours and low for another 4-5 hours. I didn't think it was going to thicken up, but the last hour it came together. Next time I might add some carrots. Great served with warm bread and perfect for cold fall nights!

I rate this recipe five stars for quick and easy preparation, flavor, nutrition, cost effectiveness, and eye appeal. I resisted the temptation to add a lot of ingredients as I was looking for a simple and pure pea soup. I added 2T Herbes de Provence, used a smoked ham shank, beef bone broth, and added no salt or pepper. Because I did not pre-soak the peas, I used an immersion blender at the end and still needed to strain the soup. I added a spoonful of the strained solids to each portion for texture and that worked for me. Next time I will pre-soak the peas and allow for more cooking time. Love it!

Wow, this was great. I used the crockpot, no oil, qt and a half vegetable broth, 3 small celery stalks and 2 medium carrots sliced very thinly, medium diced onion, 1 lb split peas and no seasonings. The Easter ham bone was flavorful enough to let the beautiful flavors of the vegetables shine through.

This was really good! Both my husband and I loved it. I made it in an Instant Pot instead. I pushed the "saute" button and then sauteed the onion in oil. I added 2 cloves minced garlic and sauteed until fragrant (only about a minute) and then added all the rest of the ingredients (chicken broth instead of water and 2 bay leaves) and cooked it on the bean/chili setting for 20 min. It was really really good!

Love this! I used the ham bone left from our Honey Baked Easter ham. I sauteed 4 cloves of garlic with diced red onion. I put the ham bone, peas, some extra finely chopped ham, about 1 Tbs. ground mustard and 1/2 tsp. of ground pepper in with equal parts water and chicken broth just to cover. I let simmer on medium heat while covered for just 1.5 hours. I then used an immersion blender to make it silky smooth. I serve mine with a dollop of sour cream! Phenomenal!..and I don't even like peas :)

So easy, flavorful, healthy, and affordable. One of our go-to's. Definitely add some carrots, celery, and few potatoes if you have them. I like other's suggestions to dump another bag of peas in midway so they are half formed for texture. Regardless, please double this recipe and add some crunchy French bread. Add a pinch of cayenne for flavor and 1/2 cup of chicken broth. No need to sauté onions ahead of time - just dump it all in. 30 min in the Instapot - easy peasy.

Good start. I brown a couple slices of chopped up bacon, then cook onion, a couple cloves of minced garlic and a chopped carrot in the bacon grease. I put this in the crock pot with the smallest shank-end ham I can find (but I love the idea of using a honey-baked ham bone.. I'll definitely try that) along with 2 outer leaves of a head of romaine lettuce, and about a teaspoon of ground black pepper. I let it cook in the crock pot on high for about 4-6 hrs, remove the ham and use my stick blender to smooth it all out. I cut up any ham left on the bone and put it back in the soup after blending, taste for salt and pepper and it's ready to eat with some crusty sour dough bread!

Soak beans in water overnight, for best results.
When soup "foams up", drain & rinse well in colander. You will have to do this a couple of times. My Grandmother said this was the GAS in the beans. 
When soup boils with a little or no foam, simmer.
After soup simmers 1 1/2 hrs. : Added Salt & pepper to taste then add 1 cup cubed ham, 2 cloves minced fresh garlic, 1 cup diced carrots , 1 cup onion and 1 cup celery. Cook about 1 more hr. Or until desired texture. 
 Orig. recipe is a good base but you need to add more "flavor"
Thank you for this basic recipe.
 (By the way, if you have Hard Water, soak & cook beans in Purchased Water (or Bottled Water). You can add 1/8 teaspoon of Baking Soda to Hard Waters, but I usually just buy water, works every time. Do not use hard water on any dried Beans.)

Good basic recipe but I think I will have to make some adjustments next time to be really good. I used a smoked ham hock and added 1 tsp. bouillon but I would add more and perhaps some garlic and carrots. I would also increase the water/broth as it was too thick, and I like thick soups! But a good starting point and not bad for my first attempt at split pea soup.
UPDATED: Tried sautéing carrots and celery with the onion, increased the water (about 6 cups) and used 4 tsp. bouillon and it was way more flavorful, with better consistency. Using a 1/2 lb. smoked ham hock and shredding the meat right before serving really helps too. So yummy, thank you!!

This was delicious. I dont really like peas but this soup was yummy! I did it in the crock pot for 6-7 hrs on high. Did not soak the peas. I used a spiral ham hock! leftover, and it did an amazing job flavoring the soup. I also sauted some garlic with the onion. I also used chicken broth instead of water and cubes. It was really good. Thanks for all the suggestions.

So easy and simple....added carrots, minced garlic and chicken stock....I wanted something else in it and thought about just garnishing with sour cream but changed it up instead with adding a little buttermilk while it was cooling. Delicious.....garnished with the ham that was left on the hock that I cooked with it.

I only added garlic and some chicken stock to the recipe. It was delicious but next time I am making a double or triple batch with carrots and celery and maybe adding some of the split peas the last hour or so of cooking. I am sure it will freeze well.
Added a little more han and garlic powder

I picked this recipe because it was the closest to what my father made when I was young. It was right on perfect! Great taste, I did add a little chicken bouillon unlike my father does, but the taste was great. 2024 Update: I still make this recipe with a tiny adjustment. I boil down the bone we have from our Holiday ham. Chunks of meat and all the remaining flavors fill the pot. No chicken broth needed! Throw in peas when ready and add the potatoes/carrots last 20 min. Done! My 20something son LOVES this. And leftovers freeze well, just add a wee bit of water and BOOM! Nice homemade soup!
Very good recipe. Added carrots, turnips, celery and onions to the split peas. Thanks for the comments on how to enhance the recipe. Still simmering.
Use this recipe all the time but also add carrots!
Very good but I added a little garlic, celery and carrots all minced. Husband loved it and wished I made more to freeze for later.😅
